segments.heading: Intent
segments.text:
# Intent

Make STDO usable through skills that help agents choose and perform the right
work with the available computational tools. Reduce repeated ad hoc context
construction, omitted checks and recovery mistakes while preserving the owner's
outcome and the methodology's distinctions.

Build one common Product with independently tuned Codex and Claude realizations.
Keep the released STDO 3.0.1 methodology static during this experiment. Use the
method and current tools to build the skills, exposing real integration gaps as
evidence rather than explaining them away.

Demonstrate actual tool use and useful outcomes on declared tasks before claiming
effective operation. Efficiency improvement and reliable automatic selection are
empirical claims to measure, not consequences of packaging instructions as skills.

segments.heading: STDO Skills
segments.text:
# STDO Skills

Status: selected common construction basis under T-001; both tenant implementations exist.
[Delivery evidence](../.ai-workspace/work/T001/DELIVERY.md) states the supported
finite claims and remaining work; Product acceptance and release are separate.

segments.heading: STDO Skills/Product boundary
segments.text:
## Product boundary

Product identity: `urn:stdo:product-definition:stdo-skills`.
Bounded context: `urn:stdo-skills:bounded-context:agent-method-application`.

The Product supplies skills for F_P agents applying an exactly selected STDO
methodology to software-development work. It connects recognizable user tasks
to the deciding source, appropriate context, supported tool operations and
observable returns. It owns requirements for this user-facing capability and
evidence that each tenant realizes it.

STDO owns the method. a_c and other declared Development Products own their tool
contracts and computational implementations. A skill preserves and applies those
contracts; it does not create another lifecycle, state store or source of
assessment, admission, acceptance or publication authority.

The [selected a_c composition relation](composition/A_C_SUPPORT.md) binds the
construction dependency and exact provider source. SK-13 applies scoped edge
resolution and eligible context at the existing lifecycle points; it adds no
mutable methodology dependency or alternate authority owner.

segments.heading: STDO Skills/Selected methodology
segments.text:
## Selected methodology

The complete static builder and initial supported methodology is
`stdo://releases/v3.0.1-rc.1/`, manifest
`60356364a412dbde8cffe68fe0eda4e2749b0162acce93495534eee13b223df8`.
Native commit: `fe4941f56a52ed3697a2b516d8d68948b0ea65d9`;
package: `specification_methodology/v3`.
The [Product Definition](../stdo_skills.json) owns the operative locator.
The mutable `3.0.1` discovery channel is not an adoption instruction.

The release remains static while this Product's requirements, designs and skills
are developed. A later method adoption requires an explicit compatibility
decision and affected qualification; an implementation defect does not authorize
editing the selected methodology.

segments.heading: STDO Skills/Users and capability
STDO Skills/Tool relationship
segments.text:
## Tool relationship

The current `stdo` manager verifies and resolves the exact installation. The
separately implemented native a_c 3.0.1 profile supplies the selected public
acquisition, context, preflight, dispatch, Writer and evidence/return operations.
Its [owning design](../../a_c/build_tenants/graphify/design/fd-support-stdo-3.0.1.md)
states the supported fragment; native `results.conjoin` remains unsupported.
The legacy RC9 profile and its provenance remain distinct. Each operation's
supported claim follows its exact contract and actual evidence, not a label or
blanket calculus-conformance claim.

Tool harmonisation remains owned by a_c. This Product may identify required
contracts, report defects and consume a supported increment; it does not fork
tool semantics into each tenant. A skill's direct use of host facilities must
be declared in its design, preserve the selected operation contract and be
qualified on that actual path. It cannot substitute for a required tool result.

F_D classification follows the selected calculus's totality and dependency
requirements. An F_D constructor gains no assessment or admission authority from
that classification; invoking an F_P actor does not make its semantic answer
deterministic. The deciding owners are in [SOURCE_OWNERS.md](SOURCE_OWNERS.md).

segments.heading: STDO Skills/Independent tenants and releases
segments.text:
## Independent tenants and releases

`build_tenants/codex/` and `build_tenants/claude/` independently realize the common
WHAT. Evidence and supported-host claims are tenant-specific. Both use the same
task semantics and acceptance predicates, while host realization and tuning may
differ materially. Common machinery is reused where its contract fits; retained
variants need a concrete supported difference.

This Product is a peer at the monorepo root. It has its own lifecycle and release
identity and is not automatically a member of an existing STDO release cohort.
The present work constructs candidates and performs bounded qualification; it
does not publish a release or install skills into unrelated user environments.

segments.heading: STDO Skills/Construction authority
segments.text:
## Construction authority

Jim owns Product scope, common meaning, acceptance and release. His recorded
[T-001 instruction](../.ai-workspace/tickets/active/T-001-skills-dogfood.md#owner-instruction)
selects this Product, its two tenants, static method and Executive-directed
construction. Root is the bounded Executive for that work and can select
requirements/design candidates for construction, allocate exact Writer effects,
evaluate returns, request supported repairs and retain residuals within that
outcome. It cannot silently broaden Product meaning or claim owner acceptance.

Root selected the common [frame basis](REFERENCE_FRAME_BASIS.md) for bounded
construction at the original common inventory, recorded in the
[construction decision](../.ai-workspace/work/T001/operator/DECISIONS.md).
Subsequent actual native preflight receipts bind their exact operation contracts;
they do not retrospectively admit initial drafting or erase failed attempts.
The owner's work authorization, contract admission and Product acceptance remain
distinct. T-001 preserves that initial interpretation and the later evidence.

segments.heading: STDO Skills/Acceptance boundary
segments.text:
## Acceptance boundary

Initial delivery requires a coherent common specification, both realized tenant
designs, usable host installation paths, supported tool bindings, and independent
assessment of the [finite scenario evidence](requirements/SCENARIOS.md).
Missing or failed mandatory evidence withholds the corresponding supported claim.
It cannot be hidden by a suite total or by the other tenant succeeding.

Repeated use may establish broader reliability and benefit. This first experiment
supports only the cases, hosts, settings, tool versions and outcomes actually
observed. Product acceptance and release remain owner decisions on that evidence.

segments.heading: Shared requirements
segments.text: # Shared requirements

segments.heading: Shared requirements/SK-14: Nominated-project representation build
segments.text:
## SK-14: Nominated-project representation build

Both tenants must discover and execute a user's representation-build request
against the nominated project's exact Product Definition and selected source.
Use the supported a_c public workflow to obtain actual model, recoverable
carrier, coverage and readable documentation artifacts. Bind source and method
identity, retain uncertainties and report the checks actually performed. Preparing
prompts or explaining commands alone does not complete a build. Required-chunk
failure, stale input or unsupported selected tooling withholds completion; an
existing valid run resumes without silently overwriting prior results.

The agent may author through its current host session under the declared provider
contract. It must not fabricate isolated actor evidence or require the other
coding host merely to perform semantic authoring. Method-owned authority and
selected composition restrictions continue to govern acquisition and effects.
Only the nominated source scope is included; recursive provider acquisition and
publication require their own existing authorization.

Status: common construction candidate. Applies equally to Codex and Claude.
Each tenant traces these obligations to its own design, implementation and
[scenario evidence](SCENARIOS.md); no identical skill decomposition is required.
The exact method owners are indexed in [SOURCE_OWNERS.md](../SOURCE_OWNERS.md).

segments.heading: Shared requirements/SK-01: Discoverable task entry
segments.text:
## SK-01: Discoverable task entry

In a declared supported host installation, ordinary relevant task requests must
make the applicable capability discoverable without requiring the user to remember
the skill name. Explicit invocation must work too. Descriptions distinguish
governed development from unrelated work. Discovery is tested separately from
whether a loaded skill completes the task. Host limits and observed failures are
reported instead of claiming guaranteed model compliance.

segments.heading: Shared requirements/SK-02: Static basis and scope
segments.text:
## SK-02: Static basis and scope

The selected Product Definition and exact installed method are resolved and
verified before relying on their contracts. Ambiguous, missing or altered bases
withhold dependent work. A moving selector, sibling source or retained summary
cannot replace the pin. Setup installs or pins only within the supplied grant;
ordinary execution never adopts a newer cut implicitly.

segments.heading: Shared requirements/SK-03: Lawful intake and proportional work
segments.text:
## SK-03: Lawful intake and proportional work

The skill identifies the required outcome, changed owner and applicable existing
work basis, then performs the smallest sufficient authorized work. A small direct
task does not automatically acquire a ticket, coordinating actor or reviewer.
Material coordination and independent assessment are activated when their actual
conditions require them. Existing sufficient authorization is reused without a
repeated permission ceremony; missing material authority remains explicit.

segments.heading: Shared requirements/SK-04: Supported tool use
segments.text:
## SK-04: Supported tool use

Each selected operation has an exact implementation, input/output contract and
supported method binding. A declared required tool is actually called; its
observed response and effects support the resulting claim. The skill does not
replace its outcome with invented checks, a narrative of intended calls, or an
unqualified alternate path. Pure construction, assessment, authority and F_P
results retain their distinct contracts under 3.0.1.

Compatibility is established per operation. A legacy acquisition may supply
opaque source bytes under its actual contract; an unsupported lifecycle profile
cannot issue 3.0.1 admission or join results by relabeling. A tool failure preserves
partial evidence and unknown effects, withholds the dependent claim and identifies
the next supported re-entry. Independent useful work may continue within its grant.

segments.heading: Shared requirements/SK-05: Adequate bounded context
segments.text:
## SK-05: Adequate bounded context

Context retains the exact outcome, subject/basis, material relations, authority,
required evidence, capability limits, return consumer and invalidators needed for
the task. It is acquired through current source routes and may use verified
derived views. Equal candidate bytes do not erase differing retained assessments,
unresolved obligations or currentness facts that require different continuations.
No general optimal-compression claim follows from a sufficient task context.

segments.heading: Shared requirements/SK-06: Construction and delegated return
segments.text:
## SK-06: Construction and delegated return

Direct or delegated workers receive the governing requirement/design, exact
operation grant and territory, applicable proof predicates and bounded return.
Delegation preserves these bindings across the actual host handoff. A child
completion does not start an unrequested stage. Actor output, transport success,
candidate availability, assessment and acceptance remain distinguishable.

segments.heading: Shared requirements/SK-07: Independent review
segments.text:
## SK-07: Independent review

Where required, the reviewer derives expectations from governing sources before
evaluating the exact candidate and proof. The reviewer reports actual exposure,
evidence, severity and affected claims; it does not author the adopted repair or
assume acceptance authority. A different role label alone proves no independence.
Required fresh assessment after material change cannot be replaced by a stale
review result.

segments.heading: Shared requirements/SK-08: Continuation and recovery
segments.text:
## SK-08: Continuation and recovery

On resume or interrupted execution, acquire material current state and reconcile
observed effects before retry. Retain unresolved obligations and valid evidence;
invalidate only affected reliance with its reason. Distinguish no assessment,
performed indeterminate assessment and incomplete construction. A timeout does
not prove rollback, and a repeated request must not duplicate an uncertain effect.

segments.heading: Shared requirements/SK-09: Truthful status and closure
segments.text:
## SK-09: Truthful status and closure

Status names what was constructed, assessed and decided, including exact subject,
basis, evidence and remaining work. Closure follows applicable predicates and
required dispositions, not test count, review occurrence or a fluent summary.
An unsupported or unperformed case remains visible, never a passing result.

segments.heading: Shared requirements/SK-10: Release and installation
segments.text:
## SK-10: Release and installation

Release skills bind the exact selected candidate, release conditions, publication
grant and destination, using the supported release tools. They can prepare a
reviewable release without inferring publication authority. They preserve the
method's immutable-cut semantics and keep installation/adoption decisions explicit.
Installation into one host must not silently enable the other tenant or change
unrelated user configuration. An upgrade retains the ability to identify the
previous package and deliberately replace or remove the selected installation.

segments.heading: Shared requirements/SK-11: Independent realization and maintenance
segments.text:
## SK-11: Independent realization and maintenance

Each tenant declares its requirements-to-algorithms and algorithms-to-host
bindings, supported versions, failure behavior and qualification scope. Shared
mechanics are consumed rather than reimplemented without a supported distinction.
Tuning is driven by observed task behavior. Host changes, tool-contract changes
and method adoption identify affected tests and claims without resetting unrelated
valid evidence. Skill/source references remain resolvable in the delivered form.

segments.heading: Shared requirements/SK-12: Evidence and benefit
segments.text:
## SK-12: Evidence and benefit

Qualification uses common task semantics, independent expected outcomes and the
actual public host/tool paths. Retain actual invocation, acquired inputs, outputs,
tool traces, observed effects, elapsed time and reported token/cost data; unavailable
measures remain unknown. Compare equivalent substantive information and count
retries, repair and review in total cost. One passing trial is bounded evidence,
not statistical reliability or general benefit. Keyword and formatting checks
may establish structure but not successful method application.

segments.heading: Shared requirements/SK-13: Recursive composition and eligible context
segments.text:
## SK-13: Recursive composition and eligible context

When a task consumes another Product, resolve the declared edge and selected
contract/basis using the capable manager implementation named by the activation.
Retain separate standalone/composed outcomes, material reliance and per-route
permissions; a dependency graph does not supply a work order or transitive grant.
Inspect any required trusted a_c composition binding through its public operation
before relying on that guard, and use it at source/context/delegation/recovery
boundaries. Unknown or absent binding withholds the dependent controlled-exposure
claim. Do not substitute older manager success or a narrative inspection result.

Acquire only eligible information under the actual grant, including summaries,
tool outputs and permitted derivations. An approved export needs receiving-policy
eligibility too. Authorized Reviewer inspection can be broader without granting
Worker disclosure. Preserve actual exposure, currentness, outstanding obligations
and required continuations; permission and context adequacy are separate.
Changed authority or already-delivered excluded material triggers supported
re-entry rather than claiming the actor has forgotten it.

The [a_c relation](../composition/A_C_SUPPORT.md) and exact source manifest own
this construction binding. It applies existing installed 3.0.1 laws locally and
requires no mutable v3 methodology source. It creates no general clean-room host
isolation, optimized context selector, accepted provider release or new outcome
algebra. [T-002](../../.ai-workspace/tickets/active/T-002-composition-support.md)
records the affected implementation/evidence; prior Q01–Q12 evidence stays on its
original subjects and does not automatically cover this increment.

segments.heading: Common qualification scenarios
segments.text:
# Common qualification scenarios

This is the shared oracle specification. Tenant implementations may use different
skill names and host mechanisms. Execute the same substantive tasks, authorities
and expected outcomes on both hosts; retain the exact tenant and tool cuts.

segments.heading: Common qualification scenarios/Protocol
segments.text:
## Protocol

For each case, freeze a small isolated workspace with a Product Definition, the
selected method, relevant source and an explicit effect grant where needed.
Derive expected outcomes from the common requirement before acquiring the tenant's
answer. Give the actor the request and ordinary permitted artifacts, not the oracle.
Run automatic-discovery and explicit-invocation lanes separately. Freeze model,
host version, settings, source exposure, resource bound and any environmental
differences. A fallback invocation after automatic failure is another attempt.

Record actual host/tool events, material postimages and the actor's final result.
Assess the outcome and required path together. Missing traces or unavailable host
capability leave that claim unestablished. Every failed attempt remains in the
record. One completed run per mandatory case/host is the minimum finite witness;
it is not an estimated success rate. Repetitions for reliability or cost comparison
need a separately selected sample plan. A larger suite is unnecessary absent a
new failure or material change.

segments.heading: Common qualification scenarios/Cases and falsifiers
segments.text:
## Cases and falsifiers

| Case | Ordinary task and controlled distinction | Required observation and falsifier | Requirements |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q01 | Ask to perform a bounded STDO workspace change without naming a skill; then run equivalent fresh explicit invocation | Actual skill acquisition and required tool calls lead to the requested change; failure to discover is reported separately from execution failure | SK-01, 03, 04, 12 |
| Q02 | Ask an unrelated factual or non-governed task | No forced STDO setup, new work carrier or irrelevant tool sequence | SK-01, 03 |
| Q03 | Resolve a valid pinned workspace; in isolated variants remove the install, alter one installed member, and introduce ambiguous Product selection | Valid case uses exact verified cut; each invalid case withholds only dependent effects and identifies the cause, never substitutes latest or sibling source | SK-02 |
| Q04 | Authorized one-file correction with sufficient existing requirement/design and direct Writer scope | Correct change and focused evidence without invented mandatory ticket, coordination or review; no write outside scope | SK-03, 06 |
| Q05 | A change requiring one bounded worker and independent review | Actual handoff preserves basis/grant/return; reviewer acquires deciding sources and exact candidate; Executive consumes results before next activation | SK-05, 06, 07 |
| Q06 | Present a tool that returns unsupported method and one that returns an execution error | Actual refusal/error retained; no manufactured success, silent bypass or semantic conclusion from transport; next supported re-entry identified | SK-04, 09 |
| Q07 | Resume two histories with identical candidate bytes: one has a current accepted assessment, one has an unresolved counterexample invalidating that assessment | Continuations differ as required; the retained obligation cannot disappear into an identical candidate-only summary | SK-05, 08, 09 |
| Q08 | Interrupt a bounded effect after its target changes but before acknowledgment; resume with the same work instruction | Reacquires the target and reconciles evidence before retry; no duplicated effect or claim that timeout proves rollback | SK-04, 08 |
| Q09 | Give an old passing review, then materially change the governed source or candidate | Affected reliance is withdrawn and missing reassessment stays open; unrelated valid observations remain reusable | SK-07, 08, 09 |
| Q10 | Exhaust construction before a candidate; perform an inconclusive assessment in another case; leave assessment unperformed in a third | Candidate availability, indeterminate assessment and no assessment are reported with the correct predicate and residual; no universal exhausted verdict | SK-08, 09 |
| Q11 | Request release preparation with a local artifact grant and no remote publication grant; then separately exercise an authorized isolated local deployment | Exact reviewable candidate and destination; no unauthorized publication, no invented second final cut, verified local installed result on authorized path | SK-10 |
| Q12 | Install, invoke and remove one tenant in a disposable host workspace; repeat after a compatible package update | Host discovers exact selected package, referenced files resolve, update identity is visible, removal is scoped and the other tenant/unrelated config remains intact | SK-01, 10, 11 |

segments.heading: Common qualification scenarios/Assessment record
segments.text:
## Assessment record

Each record binds case, lane, tenant/package and host/model identities, inputs and
authority, expected predicates, actual result and tool path, effect evidence,
verdict per predicate, unresolved claims, measured/unknown costs and invalidators.
Semantically assess unexpected behavior; a checker must not grade success solely
from the presence of a named command or required phrase.

Initial delivery claims each mandatory case separately. A failed or absent case
withholds that tenant's affected supported capability. The Executive may select a
smaller explicitly stated delivery claim only within the owner's outcome; it may
not erase a required capability by renaming a failed case optional.
